mcq: Which molecular event directly lengthens a nascent Pol II transcript?
Attack by its 3′ hydroxyl on the incoming NTP α-phosphate
Hydrolysis of ATP by XPB for every nucleotide
The attacking group is the RNA 3′ hydroxyl and the incoming nucleotide supplies its own activated phosphate. XPB acts at initiation; neither a DNA primer nor 5′ extension is required.
The main role of the short RNA–DNA hybrid in the elongation complex is to
Align the RNA 3′ end and template for catalysis
The hybrid holds the growing end in register. Older RNA exits and DNA reanneals; translation and polyadenylation are separate processes.
Which observation most directly indicates increased processivity?
A larger fraction of initiated complexes reaches the specified endpoint
More Ser5P is detected at promoters
The initial NTP incorporation rate increases
Processivity concerns sustained association and completion, not recruitment, phosphorylation or instantaneous speed.
Which component is a principal kinase of TFIIH?
CDK7 is the kinase in TFIIH; CPSF73 cleaves RNA, XRN2 degrades RNA and SPT5 is part of DSIF.
What is the consensus sequence of the Pol II CTD repeat?
YSPTSPS is an amino acid heptad. The other choices are nucleotide signals, not protein repeat sequences.
Which CTD modification is characteristically enriched near initiation in many active genes?
Ser5 glycosylation as a universal marker
Ser5P is an early transcription mark. The model does not require all early repeats to carry the same modification.
P-TEFb contains which canonical mammalian kinase?
CDK9 with cyclin T promotes productive elongation. CDK7 is associated with TFIIH and DNA polymerase δ replicates DNA.
What happens to DSIF during canonical metazoan pause release?
It is replaced by bacterial sigma
It can become elongation-supportive after phosphorylation
Phosphorylated DSIF remains associated and supports elongation. NELF generally dissociates; neither factor becomes a nuclease.
Which statement about NELF is most accurate?
It is universally required in all eukaryotes
It contributes to promoter-proximal pausing in many metazoan genes
Canonical NELF is not present in budding yeast. It stabilizes an early paused state, not bacterial termination or capping.
TFIIS primarily helps recover certain backtracked Pol II complexes by
Transcript cleavage regenerates an aligned 3′ end. TFIIS is not a DNA repair nuclease, poly(A) polymerase or histone kinase.
FACT is best classified as a
FACT helps manage nucleosomes during transcription. It is distinct from an RNA cleavage enzyme or DNA signal.
Under torsional constraint, transcription generally tends to produce
Positive supercoiling ahead and negative behind
Negative supercoiling ahead and positive behind
No local torsion in any condition
Forward movement through helical DNA can generate the twin supercoiled domains. Free rotation can reduce their buildup.
Which position normally defines the 3′ end of the upstream RNA before tail addition?
Cleavage defines the upstream RNA end. Translation stops earlier, whereas polymerase often continues farther downstream.
Which component catalyzes the canonical mammalian pre-mRNA endonucleolytic cleavage?
CPSF73 cuts the RNA internally. CDK9 phosphorylates proteins, TFIIS promotes polymerase-mediated cleavage during backtracking, and Rho is bacterial.
Which end of the downstream cleavage product is a substrate for XRN2?
XRN2 degrades the downstream RNA from its exposed 5′ end. The upstream 3′ end serves a different processing function.
The allosteric and torpedo models of Pol II termination
Both predict termination at the stop codon
Changes in elongation-complex state can facilitate exonuclease-dependent termination. Neither model depends on translation stop codons.
Which is a recognized exception to the conventional polyadenylated mRNA model?
Replication-dependent histone mRNAs typically have specialized stem-loop 3′ ends. This is not a universal property of all Pol II transcripts.
Mammalian Pol I termination commonly involves
A downstream DNA element recognized by TTF-I
The canonical Pol III oligo(dT) signal alone
TTF-I recognizes a downstream DNA terminator in the canonical mammalian Pol I system. The alternatives describe unrelated processes.
The characteristic canonical Pol III terminator is
A run of A residues on the non-template strand
A run of T residues on the non-template strand
The non-template T tract corresponds to template A and RNA U. An obligatory upstream bacterial-style hairpin is not required.
Which nuclear polymerase is typically most sensitive to α-amanitin in mammalian assays?
Pol II is highly sensitive, Pol III generally less so, and Pol I relatively resistant. Concentration and species still matter.
Its intercalation into DNA obstructs transcription. It is neither a universal Pol II-specific inhibitor nor a translation-site inhibitor.
Rifampicin mainly inhibits bacterial transcription by
Blocking the path of very short newly initiated RNA
Degrading the mature transcript from 5′ to 3′
Rifampicin binds bacterial RNAP β and restricts early transcript extension. Established elongation complexes are relatively less susceptible.
Which assay most directly reports extension by previously engaged nuclear polymerases under defined assay conditions?
A western blot of total histone
Run-on measures new RNA extension by engaged complexes. The other assays report proteins or DNA rather than ongoing RNA synthesis.
Which comparison is essential when interpreting lower Ser2P ChIP signal?
Total Pol II occupancy in the same region
Reduced Ser2P can reflect fewer polymerases or lower phosphorylation per polymerase. Total occupancy helps separate these possibilities.
ar: A: Pol II can continue transcription after pre-mRNA cleavage. R: The downstream cleavage fragment can remain associated with an elongation complex.
Both are true, and the retained downstream RNA explains continued extension after the upstream RNA has been cut.
A: High promoter-proximal Pol II occupancy guarantees high mature mRNA output. R: Polymerase occupancy depends on both entry flux and residence time.
The assertion is false. The reason is true; long residence can produce high occupancy without high productive flux.
A: Canonical Pol III termination does not require a bacterial-style upstream hairpin. R: Pol III responds to a short non-template thymidine tract.
Both are true, and recognition of this distinct signal explains why the bacterial hairpin requirement cannot simply be transferred.
A: The CTD can help coordinate RNA processing. R: DNA is read 3′ to 5′ during transcription.
Both are true, but DNA-reading direction does not explain CTD-dependent recruitment of processing factors.
A: Rifampicin generally prevents new productive bacterial transcription. R: Its major target is the bacterial ribosomal peptidyl transferase center.
The assertion is true, but the reason is false. The target is bacterial RNA polymerase.
A: All nuclear RNA synthesis ceases at every low α-amanitin concentration. R: Pol II is typically more sensitive than Pol I in mammalian assays.
The assertion is false and the reason is true. Differential sensitivity permits discrimination rather than uniform inhibition.
multi: Select the correct combination: (i) CDK7 contributes to early CTD phosphorylation; (ii) CDK9 promotes pause release; (iii) XRN2 is a DNA polymerase; (iv) CPSF73 cleaves RNA.
i, ii and iv describe transcription-associated functions. XRN2 is an RNA exonuclease, not a DNA polymerase.
Match I: Pol I, II: Pol II, III: Pol III with a: 5S rRNA, b: large pre-rRNA, c: nuclear protein-coding pre-mRNA.
Pol I makes the large rRNA precursor, Pol II the usual nuclear pre-mRNA, and Pol III 5S rRNA.
Which statements are valid? (i) TFIIS can promote RNA cleavage; (ii) backtracking can misalign the RNA 3′ end; (iii) every pause is irreversible; (iv) processivity differs from velocity.
Pauses can resolve, and backtracking may be recovered by cleavage. Processivity and velocity describe different properties.
Match the inhibitor and its principal classical target: I α-amanitin, II actinomycin D, III rifampicin; a DNA, b bacterial RNAP β, c nuclear Pol II.
The targets distinguish polymerase-selective, template-mediated and early bacterial transcription inhibition.
Which are correct? (i) Rho uses ATP-dependent RNA translocation; (ii) XRN2 degrades RNA 5′ to 3′; (iii) both are identical enzymes; (iv) both can promote termination.
The two systems share a broad pursuit principle but use different chemistry. They are not identical.
Match the readout to its most direct interpretation: I total Pol II ChIP, II run-on, III cleavage-spanning RNA assay; a engaged extension, b association, c continuous RNA across a site.
Association is not identical to extension; a cleavage-spanning assay detects an uncut molecule containing both regions.
partc: A Pol II gene has 12 kb from +1 to cleavage. Productive velocity is 2 kb/min and the early pause is 45 s. If velocity excludes that pause, when is cleavage position reached?
Transit = 12/2 = 6 min. The additional pause is 45/60 = 0.75 min, yielding 6.75 min. This predicts arrival, not necessarily actual cleavage time.
A gene is 8 kb long; v = 2 kb/min and productive entry J = 5/min. With no loss and steady state, what is mean gene-body occupancy?
Residence time = 8/2 = 4 min. N = JT = 5 × 4 = 20 complexes. Completion flux remains 5/min under the assumptions.
Entry rate is 12/min and completion probability changes from 0.8 to 0.5. What is the fractional reduction in completed transcript flux?
Before: 9.6/min; after: 6/min. Reduction = (9.6−6)/9.6 = 0.375. The probability difference of 0.3 is not the relative reduction.
Promoter signal 120 over 150 bp; gene-body signal 900 over 3,000 bp. Calculate the density-based pause index.
Densities = 0.8 and 0.3 units/bp; their ratio is 2.67. The ratio of raw counts ignores the distinct lengths.
A downstream RNA gap is 300 nt. XRN2 moves at 75 nt/s and Pol II at 50 nt/s in a hypothetical constant-rate model. How far does Pol II move before catch-up?
Relative speed = 25 nt/s; catch-up time = 300/25 = 12 s. Pol II distance = 50 × 12 = 600 nt. Real termination also depends on molecular release.
After complete synthesis inhibition, RNA declines from 640 to 80 molecules in 45 min. What is its first-order half-life?
640→320→160→80 is three half-lives; 45/3 = 15 min. The inference assumes the degradation constant is unaffected.
At steady state M = 400 molecules and k = 0.05/min. If synthesis falls to 10/min and k stays constant, what is the new steady-state abundance?
Initial synthesis = kM = 20/min. New M = S/k = 10/0.05 = 200 molecules. The transition is gradual, not an immediate halving.
A 2,500-nt RNA is elongated from an existing 100-nt nascent RNA. How many NTP incorporation events and PPi products are required for the remaining length, assuming no errors?
2,500−100 = 2,400 additions. Each adds one residue and produces one PPi. Initiation chemistry is not counted.
Hypothetical equal-length windows show promoter/body run-on signals 100/80 before treatment and 170/15 afterward. Which mechanism is most consistent?
Uniform loss of all engaged polymerases
Early signal rises while downstream signal collapses. This supports post-initiation failure; mature RNA decay alone does not directly predict the spatial run-on change.
A mutant retains correctly cleaved upstream RNA but shows increased downstream Pol II occupancy and persistent downstream RNA. Which step should be investigated first?
Cleavage still occurs, narrowing the candidate defect to post-cleavage events. XRN2 is a plausible target, not uniquely proven without rescue or direct evidence.
Reporter mutation eliminates a normal 3′ cleavage product and produces a longer RNA spanning the former site. Which conclusion is best?
RNA polymerase is absent from the cell
A translation stop codon has been created
Continuous RNA and loss of cleavage product support defective processing; further measurements of downstream transcription can test coupling to termination.
An inhibitor reduces new bacterial initiation products but permits preassembled elongation complexes to finish. Which compound best matches?
Actinomycin D as a general DNA obstruction
Rifampicin characteristically blocks the very early RNA extension pathway. The other agents either act differently or inhibit translation.
In a mammalian nuclear preparation, low α-amanitin reduces synthesis of X to 5% while Y and Z remain near 100%. Higher concentration reduces Z to 20%, Y remains near 100%. Assign X/Y/Z.
High sensitivity identifies Pol II; lesser sensitivity is consistent with Pol III; relative resistance is consistent with Pol I. Use the stated mammalian assay.
Ser2P ChIP falls by half in a gene body, and total Pol II ChIP falls by half too. What can be inferred?
Ser2 phosphorylation per enzyme certainly doubled
Ser2 phosphorylation per enzyme certainly halved
The signals alone do not establish a changed phosphorylation fraction
Pol III has replaced Pol II
The two normalized signals decline proportionally. Antibody efficiency and population averaging limit interpretation; a change in fraction is not established.
A Pol III reporter's non-template TTTTTT tract is changed to TCTGTT. The promoter is unchanged. What result is most plausible?
Disruption of the terminator tract may impair release; it does not by itself change polymerase identity or initiation.
A purified Pol II mutant extends a naked template normally but accumulates at a nucleosome-rich template; adding functional FACT improves progression. Which interpretation is strongest?
The catalytic center cannot make phosphodiester bonds
Chromatin traversal is a likely limiting step
The RNA template must be replicated
Naked-template activity and FACT rescue support a chromatin-related barrier. The experiment does not rule out every other cellular function of FACT.
An engaged backtracked Pol II makes no longer product until TFIIS is added; a shorter RNA then appears before extension resumes. What mechanism fits?
Transcript cleavage restores a catalytic 3′ end
The shorter intermediate and renewed extension are consistent with cleavage-assisted recovery. The existing complex need not initiate again.
Two samples have equal mature mRNA abundance, but sample B has twice the nascent synthesis flux at steady state. Assuming first-order degradation, what is expected in B?
M = S/k. If M is equal and S doubles, k must double in the simple model; half-life becomes half. Other assumptions must be tested in real cells.
A faster Pol II variant shows normal cleavage but transcription extends farther downstream. Which hypothesis is most reasonable?
Faster movement may make exonuclease catch-up more difficult
Pol III has been converted into Pol I
In a pursuit model, faster polymerase reduces the rate at which the exonuclease closes the gap. This is consistent, not definitive; allosteric changes can also affect release.

traps: Promoter occupancy equals gene output
Occupancy is a stock, completed transcript flux is a rate. Paused complexes can increase occupancy while output falls.
Promoter escape and pause release are identical
Escape leaves the initiation state; regulated early pausing can follow escape.
The CTD is the catalytic active center
The flexible CTD recruits and coordinates factors; the catalytic core performs nucleotidyl transfer.
CDK9 accounts for every Ser2 phosphate
Several kinases contribute. Modification patterns overlap and vary with organism and gene.
NELF is essential in every eukaryote
Canonical metazoan NELF is absent from budding yeast.
Backtracking is necessarily termination
A backtracked complex may resume synthesis, including after cleavage assisted by TFIIS.
Cleavage, polyadenylation and termination occur at one position
They are different reactions and Pol II often continues beyond the cleavage site.
XRN2 removes the upstream mRNA cap
Its canonical termination substrate is the downstream cleavage fragment with an exposed 5′ end.
Torpedo versus allosteric is an either/or choice
Altered polymerase state and exonuclease pursuit can cooperate.
Pol III requires the bacterial hairpin
The canonical Pol III signal is a non-template T tract; a hairpin is not universally required.
All Pol II mRNA has a poly(A) tail
Replication-dependent animal histone mRNAs are a classic exception.
Actinomycin D is Pol I-specific
It interacts with DNA; preferential inhibition at low doses is not absolute specificity.
Rifampicin stops every active elongation complex immediately
It predominantly blocks early extension and established complexes are relatively less susceptible.
Pol III is universally resistant to α-amanitin
Relative sensitivity varies across species and doses; typical mammalian Pol III is less sensitive than Pol II.
Higher ChIP signal proves faster RNA production
Association does not prove extension or flux; combine positional occupancy with nascent RNA measurements.
